keyframe_review.note: 69,148 km2 for 1015-1017, shape unchanged, years 1015-1016. It is too early for 1015, when Edmund still fought in the Midlands, and the page also says 'Wessex ... submitted to Cnut late in 1015'. The Cnut page, reopened: 'On 18 October 1016, the Danes were engaged by Edmund's army' (Assandun), 'all of England north of the Thames was to be the domain of the Danish prince' and 'all to the south was kept by the English king, along with London'; 'Edmund died on 30 November'. keyframe_review.note: 129,426 km2 for 1066-1071. Cliopatria cuts two pieces out of England in 1066: five cells round Hastings and Pevensey (the Duchy of Normandy row's five-cell bridgehead) and nine cells east of York. The Norman Conquest page has both as brief: 'Hardrada invaded northern England in early September', beat the English at Fulford on 20 September, York 'surrendered to him', and was defeated at Stamford Bridge on 25 September; the Normans 'landed at Pevensey in Sussex on 28 September and erected a wooden castle at Hastings', and Harold fell at Hastings on 14 October; William was crowned on 25 December 1066 and the English leaders surrendered at Berkhamsted. Neither piece is lost for 1066-1071: the Norwegians were gone in September 1066 and William took the kingdom. The 1065 shape is therefore used for 1066-1071, and the invasions are contests in the ledger. Cliopatria ends its England row in 1071 and starts Norman England in 1072. Repair 2026-10-25 (reviewer finding, agreed with the Normandy dossier): the five-cell Sussex bridgehead is drawn by duchy-of-normandy for 1066-1071 (its keyframe duchy-of-normandy_1066 and gain of 1066/10 from this state), so it is taken out of England's shape here and the ledger records the loss (1066/10, duchy-of-normandy). The rest of the 1065 shape still passes whole to William.

Ireland and Gascony are crown possessions rather than kingdom land, and Ireland has its own colony dossiers now (lordship-of-ireland, kingdom-of-ireland; notes, item 4). notes:
Written by eu-11-h on 2026-10-25 from 14 pages (the budget for a 56-shape state): Kingdom of England, Æthelstan, Eadred, Cnut the Great, Norman Conquest and Hundred Years' War (each queried twice, same page), Lordship of Ireland, First Barons' War, Conquest of Wales by Edward I, First War of Scottish Independence, Tudor conquest of Ireland, English Civil War, Lothian, List of English monarchs. Every ledger event, verdict and war cites one of them; where the page was silent the event is confidence 1 and says so.

1. ONE STATE, THREE GAPS IN CLIOPATRIA. Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of England' row is 56 shapes in 936-1708 with gaps at 1018-1045 (England sits in the North Sea Empire and Denmark-England rows), 1072-1209 (Norman England and Angevin Empire rows, both written by other parts of eu-11) and 1653-1661 (the Commonwealth row, which also holds Parliament's England and Wales in 1645-1648). The Kingdom page and the list of monarchs treat 927-1707 as one kingdom, so this dossier is one state from the unification of 12 July 927 (Cliopatria begins in 936) to the Acts of Union of 1 May 1707 (Cliopatria runs to 1708). It carries no keyframe for 1018-1041, 1072-1209 or 1649-1659 on purpose: those years are drawn by north-sea-empire and denmark-england, norman-england and angevin-empire, and commonwealth-of-england, and the ledger records the hand-overs as merge (1018, 1072, 1649) and gain (1042, 1210, 1660) events with those counterparts. If the renderers clamp shapes to the state's life they must not draw England in those years from this file. New keyframes fill what Cliopatria leaves out: 927-935 (the unified kingdom before Cliopatria starts), 1042-1045, 1645-1648 (the commonwealth-of-england dossier asks the England dossier to carry Parliament's England and Wales for those years) and 1660-1661.

2. CLIOPATRIA ROWS CORRECTED. (a) 927-959: Cliopatria draws Northumbria's 935 shape (Bamburgh to Lothian) as England from 936 but leaves York in its Danelaw row to 959; the pages have it the other way (York conquered 927; Ealdred of Bamburgh a vassal from 12 July 927; Northumbria absorbed in 954), so keyframes 927, 936, 947 and 954 swap them and the ledger has the vassal and contest events. (b) Lothian leaves in 973 (Lothian page), not 980. (c) 1015-1017: the Wessex remnant is the partition of late 1016; 1017 is the whole kingdom under Cnut. (d) 1066: the Hastings and Yorkshire cuts are September-October 1066 only. (e) 1216-1219: Prince Louis's south-east ends in 1217 (Lambeth). (f) 1305-1313: Scotland's 315 cells are an English occupation, not England. (g) 1347: Calais is English from 1347, not 1352. (h) 1431-1453: Paris goes in 1435, Normandy in 1450, Gascony in 1453, not 1440-1459; new keyframes 1436, 1450 and 1453. (i) 1558: Calais is lost in 1558, not 1579; new keyframe 1558 and 1564 corrected. (j) 1603: all Ireland is English from 1603 (new keyframe 1603-1608). (k) 1609-1639 and 1662-1707: Scotland's 322-324 cells are removed (Union of the Crowns is a personal union; the Kingdom of Scotland dossier has the matching 1609-1706 keyframe). (l) 1640-1641 Scots in Northumberland and Durham are a contest. (m) 1648-1652: the 79 Irish cells are not the kingdom's after the Commonwealth of 19 May 1649.

3. SCOTLAND DOUBLE-DRAW. Every Cliopatria shape of 1609-1639 and 1662-1708 holds all of Scotland; the Kingdom of Scotland dossier (eu-11-j) draws Scotland itself for 1609-1706. Both dossiers subtract it here, so the double drawing is gone as long as both are used.

4. IRELAND. [SUPERSEDED on 2026-10-25 by section 9: Ireland is no longer inside England's shapes.] The Lordship of Ireland (1177-1542) and the Kingdom of Ireland (1542-1800, a separate kingdom under the same crown, Kingdom page: 'Henry VIII was declared King of Ireland in 1542') now have dossiers of their own (lordship-of-ireland 1171-1542 and kingdom-of-ireland 1542-1800, both typed colony and written by another part; their notes and keyframe lists were read, their pages not). Both say that the England dossier should either subtract their keyframes or the renderer should draw the colony tint over England's shapes. This dossier does neither by editing: it keeps Cliopatria's Irish cells inside England's shapes (otherwise Ireland outside the colony keyframes would go blank) and records each Irish step as a gain or loss against a named Gaelic counterpart, mostly at confidence 1 because the Lordship and Tudor pages are almost silent on dates. The colony tint (rule 4) must win in the overlap. Open point for the reviewer: Cliopatria's England shapes hold more Irish land than the Lordship dossier's keyframes (the Pale alone in 1348-1541), so the Irish cells outside the Pale stay England's here for 1348-1539 unless they are cut. The Earldoms of Ulster (1326-1333) and Desmond (1352-1583) are recorded as vassals; the Desmond core is also inside the direct shapes from 1564 (Munster +66 cells), so the tint should win there.
